Competitor News.title: Santander and Working Title Launch Exclusive Collection for Formula 1 Fans
Competitor News.summary: Santander and Working Title Launch Exclusive Collection for Formula 1 Fans Roastbrief US
bullets: Santander, a global Formula 1 sponsor, has launched Fragmentos, a five-piece collection made with Brazilian brand Working Title, as part of its motorsport activity in Brazil. The pieces are an S Jacket, a polo shirt, a scarf, a cap and the Fragmentos Jacket, which incorporates sidepod sections from cars that previously competed in the series. The collection goes on sale from 3 November through Working Title's website.

Droga5 developed the strategy and creative concept for the collection. Singer Nicole Scherzinger, who has close ties to Formula 1, wore the S Jacket on arriving in Brazil. Santander will activate around the São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos. Santander Brasil's CMO Guilherme Bernardes said the aim is to bring Brazilian audiences closer to the worlds surrounding motorsport, reinforcing the bank's role as Formula 1's official sponsor in Brazil.
Competitor News.copy:
As a global sponsor of Formula 1, Santander is entering a new phase of its motorsport initiatives in Brazil with the launch of Fragmentos, a collection created in collaboration with Working Title, a Brazilian brand operating at the intersection of fashion, culture and community. With strategy and creative concept developed by Droga5, the exclusive pieces draw inspiration from the symbols, memories and visual codes that define the world of F1. The collection will be available beginning November 3 through Working Title’s website.

The idea was born from the emotional connection fans build with the sport. Cars, components and other elements that make their way onto the track become more than technical objects. They become physical records of races, drivers and defining moments. Fragmentos draws on this relationship, transforming symbols of the sport into pieces fans can now wear.

Wider Sports News.title: Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business
Wider Sports News.summary: After landmark partnerships with Hello Kitty, Togethxr and Monarch Commerce, the WTA is planning to expand its merchandise offering. The post Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.copy:
The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) is making its biggest move into the merchandise category in its 53-year history. At last week’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells, the tour unveiled its first-ever official merchandise collaboration with Japanese entertainment company Sanrio’s Hello Kitty to create co-branded t-shirts, sweatshirts and a collectible plush. That was followed by further partnerships with women’s sports media and commerce company Togethxr and Monarch Commerce, which will launch the tour’s first online fan shop next year.

The push into consumer products comes a year after WTA Ventures, the organisation’s commercial arm, launched a refreshed brand identity for the tour as part of a wider strategy to build a lifestyle brand that has relevance beyond the sport itself.

Wider Sports News.title: World Sailing taps Kelme as global apparel partner
Wider Sports News.summary: World Sailing taps Kelme as global apparel partner Sportcal
bullets: World Sailing has agreed a six-year commercial deal with Chinese sportswear brand Kelme, which becomes its official global sportswear partner. The agreement runs through the next two Olympic cycles, covering Los Angeles 2028 and Brisbane 2032. Kelme will design and produce apparel and technical wear for World Sailing staff, race officials and event teams at the body's biggest competitions.

The deal covers the annual World Sailing Championships, next held in 2027 in Fortaleza, Brazil (15 to 23 January) and Gdynia, Poland (22 July to 1 August), plus the Youth Sailing World Championship and the World Sailing Inclusion Championships. Kelme will also produce customised Olympic-focused clothing lines for consumers around each event and both Games. Its portfolio includes an agreement with the Asian Football Confederation running through 2029.
Wider Sports News.copy:
The World Sailing governing body has announced a new six-year commercial agreement with Kelme, the Chinese sportswear brand, which becomes the body’s official global sportswear partner.

Through the agreement, which will run through the next two Olympic Games cycles (Los Angeles 2028 and Brisbane 2032), Kelme will design and produce apparel and technical wear for World Sailing staff, race officials, and event teams at the body’s biggest competitions.

bullets: CAF has launched the search for hosts of the 2028, 2031 and 2033 Africa Cup of Nations after its executive committee unanimously decided to revert to a two-year cycle, scrapping the four-year format it announced last December. Countries must declare interest by 17 November, with full documents and government guarantees due by 8 December.

The four-year plan drew opposition over reduced commercial visibility, sponsorship inventory and playing opportunity, and CAF concluded a nations league would take too long to replace the lost revenue. Three bids had been received for 2028 before the switch, including Morocco and a joint bid from Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe. The 2027 edition will be staged across Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, and future editions will feature 28 teams.

Wider Sports News.title: Training facilities are becoming women’s sports’ next sponsorship engine, Populous report finds
Wider Sports News.summary: Training facilities are becoming women’s sports’ next sponsorship engine, Populous report finds The New York Times
bullets: A white paper from design firm Populous and advisory firm Comeback Ventures, released on Thursday, says training facilities are becoming a key sponsorship asset in professional women's sports. It cites Denver Summit FC, which converted future naming rights with CommonSpirit Health into upfront capital, and the Golden State Valkyries, whose partnership with Sephora U.S. includes naming rights to their 31,800-square-foot performance centre in Oakland.

Denver Summit used contracted CommonSpirit sponsorship payments as collateral for a loan to fund construction. The report argues legacy sponsorship models rely on metrics such as linear television viewership and static logo exposure. It cites MarketCast research that 75 per cent of NWSL fans are likely to try products from official sponsors, and 58 per cent of WNBA fans are likely to support official league sponsors. The Valkyries became the first women's franchise to pass $100m in annual revenue in their second season.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Professional women’s sports have entered a new era. A state-of-the-art training facility is now necessary for franchises to attract the best players and staff and survive in a fiercely competitive landscape. According to a white paper that global design firm Populous and advisory firm Comeback Ventures released Thursday, companies are reimagining what sponsoring these facilities looks like.

For Denver Summit FC in the National Women’s Soccer League, it meant converting their future naming rights with CommonSpirit Health to upfront infrastructure capital. In the Bay Area, the WNBA Golden State Valkyries’ landmark partnership with Sephora went beyond a naming rights deal, fueling athlete-led storytelling and player-designed fashion events. Whether sponsoring a new league such as Unrivaled or investing in a unique opportunity such as the first performance center shared by WNBA and NWSL teams, women’s sports sponsors are leveling up.

Rugby.title: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures
Rugby.summary: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures Ruck.co.uk
bullets: The 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia will expand from 20 to 24 nations, the first time that number has competed since 1999, with six pools of four. The top two in each pool and the four best third-placed teams will reach a new round of 16, so 16 nations advance. Teams play three pool matches instead of four, and champions will still play seven matches, with at least five rest days between games.

The tournament runs from 1 October to 13 November 2027 across seven Australian cities, opening with Australia against Hong Kong China in Perth. England and Wales meet in Pool F, Ireland are drawn with Scotland and Australia face New Zealand. Defending champions South Africa play Italy, Georgia and Romania, while England open against Tonga. The pool stage ends on 17 October, with the knockout stages beginning on 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
The 2027 Rugby World Cup will look very different, with the biggest overhaul of the tournament in more than two decades set to transform rugby's showpiece event. For the first time since 1999, the competition will feature 24 nations, with Australia preparing to host the biggest Rugby World Cup in history.

But the expansion is only half the story. World Rugby has introduced a completely new knockout stage, changed the pool structure and opened the door for teams finishing third to reach the last 16.

Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast is in danger of missing Saturday's Nations Championship match against South Africa after being cited for a tackle against Fiji. Prendergast will face a disciplinary process for a hip-drop tackle on Fijian captain Peceli Yato in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win in Dublin on Saturday.

The technique, when a tackling player drops their hips and bodyweight on to the ball-carrier's legs, was outlawed by World Rugby before November's internationals and the 23-year-old is the first player to be cited over its use in a game.

Rugby.title: Magnificent Wales beat New Zealand for first time since 1953
Rugby.summary: Wales celebrate a first victory against New Zealand since 1953 with a brilliant 35-28 win to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
bullets: Wales beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953, ending a run of 34 straight defeats against the All Blacks, in a nine-try Nations Championship match at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. Tries from Tomos Williams, captain Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit put Wales 35-21 ahead. New Zealand replied through Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai, with Richie Mo'unga kicking four conversions.

Wales held the All Blacks up three times over the line in the final quarter, with flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins leading the defence. The attendance of 55,152 was the lowest for the 14 Wales–New Zealand matches at the stadium. New Zealand still moved above South Africa to top the southern section with one weekend of regular matches left, after France beat the Springboks on Friday.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.

Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins.

Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: Mateo Sanguinetti Becomes Second Uruguayan Test Centurion and First Americas Prop to Reach 100 Caps
Rugby.summary: Mateo Sanguinetti Becomes Second Uruguayan Test Centurion and First Americas Prop to Reach 100 Caps Americas Rugby News
Rugby.copy:
When Mateo Sanguinetti runs onto the pitch at Trailfinders Sports Ground in London this Saturday to face Zimbabwe, the 34-year-old loose head prop will etch his name permanently into rugby history. Earning his 100th Test cap for Los Teros, Sanguinetti becomes just the second Uruguayan player, following former teammate Diego Magno, to reach the century mark, and the first prop from anywhere in the Americas to achieve the milestone.

Sanguinetti’s journey to 100 caps began in Montevideo at his beloved home club, Los Cuervos, where he started playing at age 10. After rising through Uruguay’s age-grade ranks, he made his senior Test debut against Paraguay in Asunción in April 2014. At the time, Uruguay was an amateur outfit battling to return to the global stage after missing consecutive tournaments. Sanguinetti immediately became part of the historic 2014 repechage qualifying campaign against Russia, culminating in the unforgettable victory in Montevideo that punched Uruguay’s ticket to Rugby World Cup 2015 in England and Wales.

The governing body confirmed the bans in May 2026.

The investigation found players had swapped urine samples during drug tests. Sharikadze, who captained Georgia to victory over Wales in Cardiff in 2022, has since moved into mixed martial arts and won his debut in 2026.

Rugby.summary: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into clash with Eddie Jones’s Japan The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Maro Itoje has insisted England will be ready for any curveballs Eddie Jones may throw on Saturday, warning his side they cannot “sleepwalk” into battle against Japan. Jones, England’s longest-serving head coach after his stint between 2015 and 2022, has strongly hinted he will set his side up to unsettle his former charges at Twickenham, warning that they do not like “unorthodox” rugby. The hosts are heavy favourites to back up last week’s record win over Australia with another emphatic victory and have never lost to Japan but Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes, fielding an inexperienced side against that of his predecessor.

“The overarching message this week is that we need to be alive,” said Itoje. “It’s impossible to tick off every eventuality that an opposition might do, especially a team like Japan, who have a very distinct way of playing. They’re very consistent at getting speed into the game. They could do a number of things, so let’s be alive and let’s not sleepwalk into things and think ‘most teams play like this’ because Japan aren’t most teams.

South Africa play Ireland in Dublin.

Ireland make seven personnel changes and two positional switches from the 42-12 win over Argentina, with Ronan Kelleher, James Ryan and Josh van der Flier recalled to the pack and Jamison Gibson-Park, Bundee Aki, Jamie Osborne and Tommy O'Brien drafted into the backline.

Beirne said leading the side out at the Aviva Stadium was special, with his family attending, and that Ireland want to build on last week's performance before facing world champions South Africa next week. Rugby.copy:
As Tadhg Beirne prepares to captain Ireland at home for the first time, it is worth recapping the impressive manner in which he has built up his CV in recent years. Since missing the final three games of the Six Nations Grand Slam campaign in 2023 with an ankle injury, Beirne has missed just three Ireland Tests.

He was rested against Italy in 2024 and missed last year's summer meetings with Georgia and Portugal while on British and Irish Lions duty. Such big-game ubiquity is not easily found in the modern game - and Beirne has often delivered in red and green.

Rugby.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams

bullets: Ospreys say a report they commissioned from Sheffield Hallam University concludes that Welsh rugby should not cut its professional clubs from four to three. The Welsh Rugby Union intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision due by next summer, and Ospreys and Scarlets are competing for the west Wales licence. The report covers 23 seasons from 2003-04 and says the data does not support removing a team.

The report says derbies between the four clubs generated 48% of home league attendances in Wales from 2012 to 2026 and would fall from 12 a season to six with three clubs. It also warns of a player "bottleneck". It does not address in depth how four clubs could be afforded: the WRU has reported losses of £18m and wants to cut professional spending from £26m to £20m by 2028. The full report goes to the regions and the WRU later this month.

Rugby.title: Why England’s fringe figures face World Cup audition against Japan

Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. When Eddie Jones was Steve Borthwick’s boss as England head coach, the vastly-experienced Australian explained to his assistant the concept of international rugby’s twin horizons. There is, always, the game immediately ahead, the importance of which must always be underlined to the squad. And then there is the second horizon of every cyclical sport: the World Cup, always occupying the plotting parts of a coaching staff’s minds.

It is that second horizon that has come more sharply into focus ahead of this game against Japan. Borthwick is always conscious of not getting too far ahead of himself, but, having made 10 changes and two more positional tweaks to his starting side from the win over Australia, spoke openly of the opportunity he had presented to some players. Of consideration, too, were the heavy workloads or recent injury returns for a Tommy Freeman or Fin Baxter – and that’s before even mentioning the injuries to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson, even it is hoped that the latter trio will be fit for New Zealand next week.

Rugby.title: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement
Rugby.summary: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement Americas Rugby News
Rugby.copy:
Rugby Canada and USA Rugby have launched a four-year high-performance pathway agreement to unify player development and lock in a recurring annual calendar of cross-border competition. Rather than treating one another solely as fierce regional rivals, the two governing bodies are combining resources to build a shared ecosystem of senior test matches, joint training camps, and age-grade tournaments. This alliance establishes a predictable, long-term foundation designed to elevate North American rugby on the world stage over the next decade.

The four-year high-performance pathway agreement between USA Rugby and Rugby Canada builds upon one of North America’s longest-running sporting rivalries. Dating back to the first men’s test match in 1977 and the historic first women’s test outside of Europe in 1987, the two nations have frequently clashed across regional tournaments like the Churchill Cup, the Americas Rugby Championship, and the Pacific Nations Cup. While cross-border youth tours and joint developmental programming were a regular staple of North American rugby prior to 2020, those collaborative pathways were largely neglected in the post-COVID era. As a result, the rival unions often relied on sporadic, ad-hoc fixtures rather than a unified approach to player progression.

Rugby.summary: French clubs could be set to gain another major advantage in the transfer market, with the Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) set to vote early next year on plans to allow Top 14 clubs to exclude one player from their salary cap.
bullets: The Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) will vote on 10 February on plans to let Top 14 clubs exclude one player from their salary cap. The base Top 14 cap has risen from €10.7m (£8.92m) to €11.1m (£9.2m), with limits on international player allowances, and the change could take effect as early as next season.

The Top 14 cap remains well above the Gallagher PREM's £6.4m per squad, which can stretch to £7.8m with credits. PREM clubs must spend a baseline £5.4m and may have one marquee player outside the cap, but talks on a second have stalled because seven of ten clubs must agree. In France, Toulouse and Montpellier want up to three exempt players, Clermont and Bayonne are said to be opposed, and a proposed €500,000 limit on the marquee player is a stumbling block.

Racket.summary: Siniakova and Townsend win first FAGE WTA Finals title together to cap six-title season WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Two years after falling one match short of the title at the WTA Finals, Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend got another chance to lift the trophy. This time, they made it count, defeating Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini 6-4, 6-3 on Sunday to capture their first FAGE WTA Finals title as a team and their sixth title of the season.

Siniakova and Townsend opened the week with a loss to the Italians in the group stage. Errani and Paolini, the last team to qualify for the season-ending tournament, had won all four of their matches en route to their first WTA Finals championship match. But the second seeds ended that unbeaten run on the same courts where they had won the Indian Wells title in March.

bullets: Lakshya Sen won the Kumamoto Masters Japan title on Sunday, beating home favourite Koki Watanabe 13-21 21-18 21-14 in 64 minutes. Racket.title: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set!
Racket.summary: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set! WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- We came to Indian Wells to see what Mirra Andreeva would do in her first FAGE WTA Finals. We’re leaving without ever seeing her play a third set. She won all five matches, took all 10 sets and finished the week with a 61-26 edge in games. And on Sunday, she beat the same player she’d opened against, this time with a trophy waiting for her at the end.

At 19, Andreeva’s 7-5, 6-3 win in 1 hour and 48 minutes against Elina Svitolina made her the youngest WTA Finals champion since Maria Sharapova in 2004. A straight-sets sweep on debut puts her in even rarer company. Chris Evert did it at the inaugural edition in 1972, and Serena Williams won three matches in straight sets in 2001 before taking the title by walkover.

bullets: Mirra Andreeva, 19, won the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Sunday, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 in the final. She did not drop a set across five matches and lost only 26 games, becoming the event's youngest champion in 22 years. The French Open winner rises to second in the world rankings and starts the 2027 season 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina.

Andreeva received £2.55m in prize money and a custom purple Mercedes. She beat three top-10 players on the way to the title, including Aryna Sabalenka on Wednesday, having won only one of six matches against top-10 opponents in 2026 before the event. She saved nine of the 12 break points she faced in the final. Svitolina, 32, returns to the top 10 for the first time since 2021 and finishes the year sixth.
Racket.copy:

The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week.

The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina.

Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev earned his first victory at the ATP Finals by defeating Rafael Jodar in straight sets in Turin. Zverev served supremely as he beat the rising Spaniard 6-4, 6-4 to go top of the John McEnroe group and put himself in a good position to qualify for the knockout stages.

Racket.title: Zverev claims first win as world number one at ATP Finals

bullets: Alexander Zverev claimed his first victory as world number one by beating Spain's Rafael Jodar 6-4 6-4 in the opening match of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German landed 84% of his first serves, hit 10 aces and dropped only 10 points on serve, saving two break points with back-to-back aces when serving for the first set.

Zverev, 29, lost his first match as world number one at the Paris Masters in November. He has won two majors this year and reached the Wimbledon final, with Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner both hampered by injuries. In the doubles, British player Henry Patten and Finland's Harri Heliovaara, the defending champions, beat Rafael Matos and Orlando Luz 6-3 5-7 10-4.

The victory, her second over the Czech in five WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz meetings, sends her to a third career final at the year-end championships. Having faced Andreeva earlier this week, Svitolina said she has a clearer idea of what to expect in the championship match.

Racket.title: Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva
Racket.summary: Elina Svitolina drops just three games as she thrashes Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva.
bullets: Elina Svitolina beat Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in 64 minutes to reach the WTA Finals final in Indian Wells, where she will face Mirra Andreeva. The Ukrainian lost her opening group match to Andreeva but then won three in a row, including against Aryna Sabalenka, ending a six-match losing streak against her. It is Svitolina's third final at the event, after winning the title in 2018.

Svitolina is back in the top 10 for the first time since October 2021 and has 11 wins over top-10 opponents this year, the most on the WTA Tour. Andreeva, 19, beat Jessica Pegula 6-3 6-4 to become the youngest finalist since Maria Sharapova in 2004. She has not dropped a set and has lost just 18 games, the fewest for a finalist since the round-robin format began in 2003.
Racket.copy:
Elina Svitolina dropped just three games as she thrashed Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva. Ukraine's Svitolina was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes.

It caps a remarkable turnaround for world number six Svitolina in Indian Wells, having suffered a heavy defeat in her opening group match against Andreeva. However, she has shown all of her fighting spirit to win her next three matches, including snapping a six-match losing streak to Aryna Sabalenka on Friday.

Racket.title: Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals
Racket.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's season ends in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beats the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals.
bullets: Aryna Sabalenka's season ended at the WTA Finals as Elina Svitolina beat her 6-3 3-6 6-1 to reach the semi-finals. Sabalenka forced a deciding set but lost the last six games, two days after losing the final 11 games against Mirra Andreeva. Svitolina, 32 and the 2018 winner, will meet Czech world number eight Linda Noskova in the last four.

Sabalenka lost the finals at both the Australian Open and the US Open, so 2025 is her first season since 2022 without a major. She won three other titles, including the Indian Wells and Miami double, and had the tour's best win percentage at 81% (47-11). Elena Rybakina took the world number one ranking from her after 99 weeks. Andreeva, 19, beat Diana Shnaider 6-2 6-1 to complete a perfect group record and faces Jessica Pegula in the other semi-final.
Racket.copy:
Aryna Sabalenka's season ended in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beat the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals. Sabalenka took her frustration out on her racquet and reacted to losing a point by crouching to the ground at the back of the court as a semi-final place slipped away.

The Belarusian was able to force a deciding set after unravelling in the latter stages of the first, but lost the final six games in slumping to a 6-3 3-6 6-1 loss. It came two days after the four-time major winner lost each of the last 11 games as she was thrashed by Mirra Andreeva.

Racket.title: Jessica Pegula wins thrilling contest at WTA Finals, Coco Gauff eliminated
Racket.summary: Jessica Pegula wins thrilling contest at WTA Finals, Coco Gauff eliminated Al Jazeera
bullets: Jessica Pegula saved a match point to beat Linda Noskova 7-6 (7/2), 4-6, 7-5 on Thursday and reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, eliminating fellow American Coco Gauff. The match lasted two hours and 45 minutes. Pegula hit a career-high 16 aces and Noskova a career-high 15 double faults. The tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells due to the United States-Israel war on Iran.

Noskova, Gauff and Pegula all finished 2-1 in the group, with Noskova winning it on sets 5-2, ahead of Pegula (5-3) and Gauff (4-3). Gauff earlier beat Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5, winning six straight games from 1-5 down in the second set. Pegula now meets Mirra Andreeva in Saturday's semi-finals, having apologised for earlier remarks about Andreeva that were livestreamed.
Racket.copy:
Jessica Pegula saved a match point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7/2), 4-6, 7-5 win over Linda Noskova on Thursday to advance out of her round-robin group at the WTA Finals and send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships.

Pegula had a career-high 16 aces while Wimbledon champion Noskova had a career-high 15 double faults in a see-saw battle that spanned two hours and 45 minutes at the tournament, which was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells due to the United States-Israel war on Iran.

Racket.summary: Siniakova, Townsend seal semifinal berth; Errani, Paolini stay unbeaten at FAGE WTA Finals WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
Second seeds Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend booked their spot in the semifinals of the FAGE WTA Finals on Thursday, joining Italians Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini, who completed an unbeaten run through the Group 2 round-robin stage with their third consecutive victory.

In the decisive match for the second semifinal berth from Group 2, Siniakova and Townsend took the opening set 6-2 against Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez. The Czech-American duo led 4-2 in the second set when Melichar-Martinez was forced to retire because of an injury.

Racket.title: Pegula saves match point to beat Noskova & reach WTA Finals last four
Racket.summary: A determined Jessica Pegula saves match point to beat Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and reach the WTA Finals last four at the expense of Coco Gauff.
bullets: Jessica Pegula saved a match point to beat Linda Noskova 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 7-5 and reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, knocking out Coco Gauff. Noskova led by a break in the third set and held a match point at 5-4 on Pegula's serve. Pegula hit 16 aces, her most in a WTA Tour match, while Noskova hit 15 double faults.

Pegula will face French Open champion Mirra Andreeva for the first time in the last four, while Noskova, already through, plays Elina Svitolina or Aryna Sabalenka on Saturday. Gauff had earlier beaten Marta Kostyuk 6-4 7-5 despite a lower back problem, rallying from 5-1 down in the second set. Kostyuk, a late call-up after Elena Rybakina withdrew, was hampered by a wrist injury.
Racket.copy:
A gritty Jessica Pegula saved a match point to beat Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and reach the WTA Finals last four at the expense of Coco Gauff. Pegula knew she would have to beat Noskova to advance after Gauff's victory over Marta Kostyuk earlier on Thursday.

The American showed great mental resilience throughout a fluctuating match to win 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 7-5. Noskova had gone a break up in the third set and held a match point on Pegula's serve at 5-4, but could not take it.

Racket.title: Gauff beats Kostyuk but falls short of FAGE WTA Finals semifinals
Racket.summary: Gauff beats Kostyuk but falls short of FAGE WTA Finals semifinals WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Coco Gauff knew coming into Thursday that even a win over Marta Kostyuk might not be enough to keep her in the FAGE WTA Finals. What she could do was give herself a reason to watch the second match. And for a while in the second set, even that looked like it would take some doing.

Gauff beat Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5, winning the last six games to finish 2-1 in round-robin play. But her bid for a semifinal spot ended later Thursday when Jessica Pegula beat Linda Noskova 7-6(2), 4-6, 7-5. Noskova won Group 1, and Pegula took the second semifinal spot on percentage of sets won.

Racket.title: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high
Racket.summary: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
ATP has delivered its strongest partnership performance to date, with central partnership revenues rising 49% year on year in 2026. The increase sees ATP central partnership revenues surpass the $100 million mark for the first time. Since 2022, revenues have increased by more than 200%, driven by new agreements and expanded investment from longstanding partners such as Emirates, Infosys, Nitto, Lexus, Haier and Yokohama, some of which have worked with ATP for more than a decade.

This year’s growth was fuelled by new partnerships with EQT and K-Swiss, alongside continued investment from existing partners. Earlier this week, ATP also announced a multi-year partnership with Julius Baer, which becomes ATP’s first Official Wealth Management Partner and the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, with activation across five ATP tournaments on three continents from 2027.

Racket.title: Paralympic medallist Shuker ends 24-year tennis career
Racket.summary: British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker retires after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.
Racket.copy:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals. The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season. At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

Racket.title: Lakshya, Srikanth Reach Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 Quarterfinals
Racket.summary: Lakshya, Srikanth Reach Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 Quarterfinals Sportscape Magazine
Racket.copy:
Lakshya Sen beat Dong Tian Yao and Kidambi Srikanth upset World No.8 Kodai Naraoka to reach the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 quarterfinals. See the scores. India had a great outing at the Kumamoto Masters 2026 in Japan, with Lakshya Sen and Srikanth Kidambi winning their pre-quarterfinals at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium. Sen and Kidambi, who recently got promoted in the BWF World Rankings, have now reached the BWF Super 500 quarterfinals. World No.13, Lakshya, beat China’s Dong Tian Yao, 2-0, and World No.31, Kidambi, produced the biggest upset, defeating World No.8, Japan’s Kodai Naraoka, 2-1. The Japan Masters 2026 are an important stepping stone towards the BWF World Tour Finals, which are scheduled in December.

India’s No.1 shuttler in the men’s singles event won against World No.45, Dong, 21-8, 21-14. Sen dominated in both sets, winning the Super 500 quarterfinals. Before Dong, Lakshya won against Chinese Taipei’s Chi Yu Jen, 21-19, 21-18 in 49 minutes. The 25-year-old won the Hylo Open men’s singles title in Germany in October. The win takes the Indian one step closer to the Japan Masters title, which India is yet to win since its beginning in 2023.

bullets: Great Britain has been drawn in Group D of the 2027 United Cup, alongside France and host nation Australia. The 10-day event runs from 1-10 January in Perth and Sydney, with 18 nations in six round-robin groups. Group D ties will be played at the Ken Roswell Arena in Sydney from 2-6 January.

Emma Raducanu and British No.1 Arthur Fery lead the GB squad, which also includes Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski, Olivia Nicholls and Neal Skupski. It will be Raducanu's first tournament back after six months out with injury. The top six teams and two best runners-up reach the quarter-finals on 7-8 January, with the final on 10 January. GB has reached the quarter-finals twice since 2023.
Racket.copy:

The 10-day competition will see 18 nations compete across six round-robin groups, with the top six teams and two best-performing runners-up progressing to the quarter-finals. Ties are played as a best-of-three format, including one women’s and one men’s singles match and one mixed doubles rubber.

Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu has finally confirmed her return to competition at the United Cup after spending months sidelined by a shin injury. The 23-year-old will represent Team GB along with British No. 1 Arthur Fery, and they face France and Australia in the group stages at the beginning of January. Raducanu has not played a match since she lost the Queen's final to Donna Vekic in mid-June. She subsequently pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament and has given little updates on her comeback since.

But Raducanu's lengthy absence has paid off, as she has spent enough time sidelined by injury to get a protected ranking. This is offered to players who have been out for six months, and is based on their ranking before their absence. It can be used to enter up to eight tournaments, including two Grand Slams.

Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Just like their past two meetings, Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova's second round-robin match at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals went to a third set. Wednesday, in their third straight meeting to go to a decider, Svitolina edged Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and will have a chance to compete for a semifinal spot in Friday's group stage finale against [2] Aryna Sabalenka. Muchova falls to 0-2 at the competition, and is eliminated from advancing to the semifinals as a result of Mirra Andreeva's win.

With the comeback, she ended Muchova's impressive 32-0 unbeaten record this season after taking the first set -- 26 of those wins had come in straight sets and six in three sets. Svitolina improves to 19-5 in three sets this season, while Muchova dropped just her third deciding set of 17 this year.

bullets: Emma Raducanu will return to tennis at the United Cup in Australia, which runs from 1 to 10 January 2027. The 23-year-old lost the Queen's Club final to Donna Vekic on 14 June and withdrew from Wimbledon on the eve of her opening match 14 days later. She will play for Britain alongside Arthur Fery, with group matches against Australia and France in Sydney.

By delaying her comeback, Raducanu can use a special ranking of 38, available to players out injured for at least six months, to enter eight events in 2027. These include two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 tournaments. Her actual ranking of 107 would probably be too low for the Australian Open main draw. She has averaged 31 matches a season since her 2021 US Open win and played 21 in 2026.

Racket.title: Give Me the Ball! review – tennis trailblazer Billie Jean King is ferocious force for equality
Racket.summary: Sparky and engaging documentary about the ‘battle of the sexes’ player, who fought her whole career to ensure the women’s game got the respect it deserved After the engaging Evert and Navratilova documentary Chris and Martina: The Final Set comes this watchable and engaging documentary portrait of Billie Jean King. It includes sparky talking-head contributions from the woman herself, in her vivid red glasses, one of many sets that she apparently carries in a separate accessory case – perhaps the influence of her old friend Elton John. There is also, of course, ample (if familiar) archive footage of her amazing climb to greatness and pop-cultural political importance. And as always with tennis documentaries, it is the British viewers, not the Americans, who can appreciate the unmistakable BBC-commentating voice of Dan Maskell. King (née Moffitt) was a ferocious force in women’s tennis from the 60s onwards and a vehement but polite advocate for equal rights on prize money. The women’s game was equally skilful, though not possessed of the same brutal brawn-power, and sold as many stadium seats. King sensationally helped to launch the Virginia Slims women’s tour – one of the great commercial revolutions in US sports, and had to work hard on promotion and sponsorship at the same time as simply training and playing. And while all this was happening, she had to come to terms with her gay sexuality, while married to the poignantly devoted Larry King, who is a gallantly supportive interviewee here. Racket.title: WTA Finals: Linda Noskova beats Coco Gauff to reach semi-finals, Jessica Pegula wins
Racket.summary: WTA Finals: Linda Noskova beats Coco Gauff to reach semi-finals, Jessica Pegula wins BBC
bullets: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova beat Coco Gauff 6-3 6-3 to become the first player to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals, on her tournament debut. The 21-year-old Czech broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set, made only one unforced error in the second and sealed victory with an ace. It was her sixth top-10 win of the season.

Gauff hit eight aces and eight double faults and won only six of 24 points behind her second serve, but she can still qualify for the last four, as can Jessica Pegula. In group one, Pegula beat alternate Marta Kostyuk 6-2 7-5 for her first win since September. LIV confirmed two weeks ago that it will wind down operations four years after launching and spending more than $5bn. Several LIV players have struck deals for 2027, and Joaquin Niemann and Lucas Herbert have reportedly agreed to play at least 15 events each through wild cards. Kinnings said stronger fields would arrive at a time of year when dual members are in the United States, benefiting promoters, sponsors and broadcasters. Bryson DeChambeau is eligible for 2027 as a recent major champion, and a membership announcement is expected on Tuesday. Kinnings said the tour is in "very positive" talks with the PGA Tour, which from 2028 will run a two-tier structure with top-tier purses of at least $20m, and hopes for news by the New Year.

The invites are likely to fall between February and August and will not include the Rolex Series events.

The 28-year-old has no tour status but can play the circuit because it has offered packages of guaranteed invites to non-members returning from LIV. He remains banned on the PGA Tour until at least next August. Lucas Herbert is also set to sign a similar deal. The tour will confirm on 17 November whether Bryson DeChambeau, eligible through his 2024 US Open win, has taken a card for 2027.
Golf.copy:
A number of LIV Golf stars are converging on the DP World Tour, including the breakaway league’s most successful player. He earned $88million in prize money across his five seasons yet still did not top the inordinate earnings table at LIV Golf. But there can be no doubt that, with his nine individual victories, Joaquin Niemann was the most successful player on the now-doomed breakaway league.

What the Chilean’s dominance during this period will mean for his legacy can and will be disputed, but Niemann is returning to golf’s traditional tours as a winner on LIV, the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour.

Golf.title: First win for Duncan after 12 years & 222 attempts
Golf.summary: American Lindy Duncan wins The Annika for her first LPGA Tour title after playing in 222 events over 12 years.
bullets: American Lindy Duncan, 35, won her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd attempt at The Annika, finishing 16 under after a final-round 67 at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida. She began the day one shot ahead and was tied with South Korea's Choi Hye-jin with two holes left, before two late birdies secured a two-shot victory. Duncan joined the tour in 2014 and had only one top-10 finish this season.

The win lifted Duncan from 74th to 34th in the season-long points race, qualifying her for the 60-player CME Group Tour Championship. World number one Nelly Korda finished seventh and will aim to win a second title of the season at the finale next week. England's Lottie Woad, also in the field for the finale, secured a top-10 finish. Duncan said she was "completely shocked" and thanked those who believed in her.
Golf.copy:
American Lindy Duncan was left "completely shocked" after winning her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd time of asking. The 35-year-old started Sunday's final round of The Annika with a one-shot lead and two late birdies saw her claim victory.

Duncan, who joined the tour in 2014, had only enjoyed one top-10 finish this season. But her three-under-par 67 saw her finish on 16 under at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida, two shots clear of her nearest challenger, South Korea's Choi Hye-jin .

Golf.title: 'I'm back': Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards
Golf.summary: Ten players earned PGA Tour cards via the DP World Tour on Sunday, including Patrick Reed, ex-LIV pros and a former delivery driver. The post ‘I’m back’: Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Patrick Reed has secured a PGA Tour card for 2027 via the DP World Tour's season-long points race, which offers 10 cards. He finished second among players without full PGA Tour status, behind Eugenio Chacarra, who took the top spot and will also be in early Signature Events and the Players Championship. Reed left LIV earlier this year. He won in Dubai and Qatar and finished T2 in Bahrain, plus a T12 at the Masters and T10 at the PGA Championship.

The future of the 10-card pathway is uncertain, with the DP World Tour-PGA Tour alliance up in the air. Competition is expected to increase in 2027 with an influx of former LIV players. Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship on Sunday and finished third in the Race to Dubai, but was ineligible for a card because of his LIV season. Reed said the decision to leave LIV came with only one year to qualify, and that returning would let him play closer to home.
Golf.copy:
On Sunday in Dubai, Patrick Reed made it official. “I’m back,” he said as he accepted a metal PGA Tour card and flashed a wide grin. “It feels good.” Reed left LIV earlier this year and, facing a one-year ban from the PGA Tour, turned his attention to the DP World Tour, where he hoped to earn one of 10 PGA Tour cards available via the season-long points race.

He took the drama out of that quest in just a few tournaments, winning in Dubai, finishing T2 in Bahrain and winning in Qatar in three consecutive early season events. Add in a T12 at the Masters and a T10 at the PGA Championship and he’d wrapped up his return pre-summertime.

bullets: Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates by five shots, closing with a six-under 66 for his ninth DP World Tour title. He finished the season third in the Race to Dubai behind Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra, having entered the two season-ending play-offs outside the top 50 after mainly playing LIV Golf this year.

The win lifts Hatton to second in the European Ryder Cup rankings ahead of next year's centenary contest at Adare Manor, and he said he wants to be on Luke Donald's team. It is the fourth win in six DP World Tour events for a former LIV Golf player, following Adrian Meronk, Chacarra and Jon Rahm. The new season starts at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from 26 to 29 November in Sydney.

The win sees him end the DP World Tour season third in the Race to Dubai rankings, behind Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra, having entered the two season-ending play-offs outside of the top 50 after predominantly playing on LIV Golf this year.

The announcement follows the conclusion of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, where Tyrrell Hatton secured a five-shot victory and Rory McIlroy was crowned Race to Dubai champion for a joint-record eighth time and fifth consecutive season.

Golf.title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy snatches Race to Dubai title as Tyrrell Hatton claims big win in season finale
Golf.summary: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy snatches Race to Dubai title as Tyrrell Hatton claims big win in season finale Sky Sports
bullets: Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates by five shots, finishing on 15 under after a closing six-under 66 that included four birdies in a six-hole stretch on the back nine. It was his ninth DP World Tour title and his sixth Rolex Series win, a week after finishing runner-up at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

Rory McIlroy finished second after a bogey-free 67 and overtook Eugenio Chacarra in the standings to win the Race to Dubai for a fifth successive season. It was his eighth Order of Merit title, matching Colin Montgomerie's record. Chacarra, who shared third on eight under with Oliver Lindell, narrowly missed out. The new season starts at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from 26 to 29 November, and McIlroy's next event is the Australian Open from 3 to 6 December.
Golf.copy:
Tyrrell Hatton stormed to a five-shot win at the DP World Tour Championship, where Rory McIlroy snatched Race to Dubai victory from Eugenio Chacarra. Hatton took a one-shot lead into the final day at Jumeirah Golf Estates and never relinquished top spot, pulling clear of the field with four birdies in a six-hole stretch on the back nine.

The Englishman posted a six-under 66 to end on 15 under and claim a ninth DP World Tour title, as McIlroy leapfrogged Chacarra in the season-long standings with a runner-up finish after a thrilling Sunday tussle.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka And Ludvig Aberg Headline RSM Classic Field As Battle For PGA Tour Cards Reaches Climax
Golf.summary: Stars including Koepka and Aberg will play in the final event of the PGA Tour season, as well as players battling for full playing privileges
bullets: Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka and former champion Ludvig Aberg are in the field for the RSM Classic, the final PGA Tour event of the season, at Sea Island Golf Club in Georgia. Koepka makes his first PGA Tour start since finishing T67 at the Wyndham Championship in August, while Aberg seeks a second title after winning the event in 2023.

Following the tournament, only the top 100 in the rankings not otherwise exempt will earn full PGA Tour playing privileges for 2027, so many players have more at stake than usual. Matt Wallace, Christiaan Bezuidenhout, Max Greyserman, Billy Horschel and Lucas Glover are among those still uncertain of a place. Defending champion Sami Valimaki, Keegan Bradley, Brian Harman and Michael Brennan, who has two wins this year, are also playing.
Golf.copy:
Five-time Major winner Brooks Koepka and former champion Ludvig Aberg are among the big names in the field for the final PGA Tour event of the season, the RSM Classic. The tournament, which takes place at Sea Island Golf Club in Georgia, will also see several notable names battling to secure full PGA Tour status for 2027 as the FedExCup Fall concludes.

Koepka will be making his first PGA Tour start since placing T67 at the Wyndham Championship in August. Meanwhile, Aberg will be hoping to win the RSM Classic for the second time, having claimed his maiden PGA Tour title at the event in 2023.

Tom Lewis can tell you all that’s happened to him over the past couple of weeks at DP World Tour Qualifying School. It’s just that the 35-year-old Englishman thinks because it’s so unreal, the words may fall short.

“Yeah, I mean, these things happen,” Lewis said, “you can’t write it.” – The exit. Across a 15-year pro career, Lewis has seen some success. A pair of DP World Tour wins. A Korn Ferry Tour win. He’d also played on a Walker Cup team, and he was the low amateur at the 2011 Open Championship. But this year, he played mostly on the Hotel Planner Tour, the circuit below the DP World Tour, and finished 89th in the season-long points race. He entered Q-School. Maybe he’d make a run. Golf.title: The rise and fall of LIV Golf: How a $5 billion illusion met reality
Golf.summary: The rise and fall of LIV Golf: How a $5 billion illusion met reality The New York Times
bullets: LIV Golf admitted defeat on 5 November and has begun winding down its operations following a bankruptcy filing, after a scramble to find a new funding partner. CEO Scott O'Neil was told to shut the league down less than 16 months after a January 2025 meeting in Saudi Arabia, where chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan of the Public Investment Fund told him he had all the time he needed.

Under former CEO Greg Norman, billions were spent while a lack of revenue cost the league hundreds of millions in its first three years. The piece puts total spending at about $5bn. Jimmy Dunne, who negotiated the June 2023 framework agreement with the PGA Tour, said LIV had lost its funding backer, the near-trillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund.
Golf.copy:
In his first month on the job, LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil flew to Saudi Arabia to learn just how much time he had. O’Neil met with his new boss, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and LIV’s chairman, to discuss the situation their league faced. Under former CEO Greg Norman, billions had been spent, but a shocking lack of revenue cost the league hundreds of millions in its first three years.

During the January 2025 meeting, O’Neil laid out two paths, according to multiple sources briefed on the meeting who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to do so publicly. One would be painful — dramatically trim the league’s exorbitant expenses, lay off employees, and do everything possible to get the balance sheet under control immediately. The other was a seven-year plan, built around maintaining LIV’s structure but gradually squeezing costs.

Golf.summary: Entry list for DP World Tour season-opener offers early ex-LIV flavour Irish Golfer Magazine
bullets: The entry list is out for the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club in Sydney, the 2027 DP World Tour season-opener, which tees off on 26 November. Thomas Pieters, Michael La Sasso and Carlos Ortiz have received invitations, the first former LIV Golf players to be offered DP World Tour invites for 2027.

Pieters missed out at Q School's final stage, while La Sasso, who won LIV's final event in Indianapolis in August, exited at the second stage. Tom McKibbin and David Puig, who retained their DP World Tour membership during their LIV spells, are also in the field, as are Cam Smith, Elvis Smylie and Harold Varner III. The invitations form part of an olive branch from tour officials to players leaving LIV without retained status after dual membership ended.
Golf.copy:
The curtain is only halfway down on the DP World Tour’s season-finale in Dubai, but the entry list is already out for the 2027 season-opening BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club in Sydney, teeing off on November 26th.

Liam Nolan makes his debut as a card-carrying DP World Tour member after an impressive HotelPlanner Tour campaign that saw him claim a maiden professional win at the Abu Dhabi Challenge, while Tom McKibbin makes his return to full-time DP World Tour action after opting out of any future LIV Golf involvement.

Golf.title: McIlroy and Hatton tied as Chacarra stays in hunt
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy is tied for the lead at the halfway mark of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship as he chases a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title.
bullets: Rory McIlroy is tied for the lead with England's Tyrrell Hatton at the halfway stage of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai. McIlroy followed an opening 69 with a 70, while Hatton shot 69 after five birdies and two bogeys. Joost Luiten (73) and Norway's Kristoffer Reitan lie one shot back.

McIlroy is guaranteed to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Race to Dubai titles with victory this week, and sits four shots ahead of standings leader Eugenio Chacarra, who is one under. Hatton, who finished second behind Jon Rahm in Abu Dhabi last week, is chasing a first DP World Tour win since leaving LIV Golf. McIlroy said scoring this week was not as good as in previous years because of the course set-up.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy is tied for the lead at the halfway mark of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship as he chases a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title. The six-time major winner followed a three-under opening 69 with an up-and-down 70 to join England's Tyrrell Hatton at the top at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai.

Hatton mixed five birdies and two bogeys to shoot 69, while overnight leader Joost Luiten carded a 73 to lie one shot back alongside Norway's Kristoffer Reitan. McIlroy, who is guaranteed to equal Colin Montgomerie's record haul of eight season-long crowns with victory this week, sits four shots ahead of Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra.

Golf.title: The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots
Golf.summary: The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots Sky Sports
bullets: World No 1 Nelly Korda returned to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence with a bogey-free seven-under 63 at Pelican Golf Club in Florida. That leaves her two shots behind leaders Minami Katsu of Japan and South Korea's Hye-Jin Choi after the opening round of The Annika. Lindy Duncan, who made a hole-in-one in her round of 62, is also ahead of Korda on eight under.

Korda's last competitive golf was the Solheim Cup in September, and she said she was burned out afterwards and needed to step away mentally. She has already clinched LPGA player of the year on points, and can qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame with a win in either of the final two events of the season. England's Lottie Woad and Ireland's Leona Maguire are tied for ninth on five under, with Charley Hull a shot further back.
Golf.copy:
World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead. Korda, whose last competitive golf came at the Solheim Cup in September after her most recent LPGA Tour outing in August, shot a bogey-free seven-under par round of 63 at Pelican Golf Club in Florida.

Korda trails Japan's Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin Choi by two shots, with fellow American Lindy Duncan also ahead of her on eight under after making a hole-in-one during her 62.

Golf.title: NBC Golf Announcer Dan Hicks Dies Aged 64
Golf.summary: NBC Golf Announcer Dan Hicks Dies Aged 64 Golf Monthly
Golf.copy:
Legendary sports broadcaster Dan Hicks, one of the most well-known voices in golf, has died at the age of 64. The NBC Golf play-by-play announcer had been in his role since 2000 and commentated on a vast number of iconic moments within the sport such as Tiger Woods' famous 2008 US Open triumph and JJ Spun's 64-foot monster putt at Oakmont in 2025.

Hannah Storm, Hicks' wife and fellow announcer, confirmed his death in a statement on Thursday. Storm shared that Hicks had been suffering with an "acute illness" but his passing was "sudden" and unexpected. He is survived by his wife and three children.

The world No 2 is chasing an eighth Race to Dubai title and a fifth in a row, which would equal Colin Montgomerie's tally of eight Order of Merit wins.

Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley said McIlroy generally delivers when he has a clear goal, and described the title race as a three-horse contest between McIlroy, Chacarra and Rahm. Nine players began the week with a mathematical chance, but Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper, Aaron Rai and Ryan Fox all made poor starts. Golf.title: LPGA to update pace-of-play policy with stricter punishments
Golf.summary: The LPGA is updating its pace-of-play policy and dishing out stricter punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season. The post LPGA to update pace-of-play policy with stricter punishments appeared first on Golf .
bullets: The LPGA will introduce stricter pace-of-play punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season. Players will be fined immediately for taking one to five seconds over their allotted time, with the two warnings removed, while one-stroke (six to 15 seconds) and two-stroke (16 seconds or more) penalties will now also carry a fine.

A player reaching 35 timed holes will be fined, down from 40, and the time allowed per shot falls from 70 to 60 seconds. Players were told at The Annika in Belleair, Florida. There were five one-stroke and two two-stroke penalties this year, against three and two in 2025. Nelly Korda and Charley Hull backed the changes, and the season ends next week at the CME Group Tour Championship.
Golf.copy:
The LPGA is updating its pace-of-play policy and dishing out stricter punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season. Players were informed of the changes by the Pace of Play Committee during a Tuesday meeting at The Annika in Belleair, Florida, the LPGA’s penultimate event of the season.

The updated policy will include more fines. Previously, players who took one to five seconds over their allotted time to hit a shot were given two warnings before a fine. Now the warnings are gone and players will be fined right away. Six to 15 seconds over allotment remains a one-stroke penalty but a fine will now be included, and 16 seconds or more remains a two-stroke penalty but will also come with a fine.

bullets: LIV Golf's lawyers told a bankruptcy court last week that the league would begin winding down toward liquidation and that LIV Golf 2.0 would not go ahead. Eight former LIV players are in the field at this week's DP World Tour Championship, and Eugenio Chacarra, Patrick Reed and Jon Rahm all have a chance of winning the Race to Dubai.

Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and others have DP World Tour status for 2027, while Reed and Chacarra will head to the PGA Tour but plan to play in Europe too. Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is dead. The time of death for the rebel league came last week in a bankruptcy hearing, when LIV’s lawyers informed the court they would begin winding down toward liquidation and that LIV Golf 2.0 would not go forward as they hoped.

While the former Saudi-backed league will soon fade into golf history, the remnants of it are all over the tour it tried “to destroy.” “They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race,” Rory McIlroy said last week in Abu Dhabi about LIV’s threat to the DP World Tour. “They were going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy the European Tour.”

Golf.title: These 20 players just earned a DP World Tour card as LIV Golf stars dominate at Q School
Golf.summary: These 20 players just earned a DP World Tour card as LIV Golf stars dominate at Q School Today's Golfer
Golf.copy:
It’s one of golf’s most grueling tests and it’s over for another year. For these players, Europe’s top table awaits in 2027… The DP World Tour Q School results are in. Teeing up at Infinitum in Spain this week were 156 hopefuls who would play 108 holes over six days in a bid for DP World Tour playing rights next season. This year’s chances were ever so slightly slimmer, with the number of available cards reduced from 20 to 15 plus ties. As it happened, 20 players did exactly that, so who booked their ticket for 2027?

Josele Ballester carded six rounds of 68 or better to finish on 32-under-par to top the leaderboard alongside fellow Spaniard Rocco Repetto-Taylor. Ballester, who joined the professional ranks last year to join Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs team on LIV Golf, made north of $10 million in two years on the league before it was wound down.

Golf.title: Ferguson targets PGA Tour after injury woes
Golf.summary: Ewen Ferguson believes he is capable of competing for a place on the PGA Tour and has set his sights on bigger achievements in 2027 after putting an injury-hit spell behind him.
bullets: Scotland's Ewen Ferguson, a three-time DP World Tour winner, says he believes he can compete for a place on the PGA Tour after putting an injury-hit spell behind him, ahead of this week's season finale in Dubai. The 30-year-old, making his fifth consecutive appearance at the event, cites improved fitness, greater strength and a lower scoring average than in any other year, though his putting has held back his challenges for titles.

Ferguson has spent four months working with gym coach Kenny McKenzie and travels with a physiotherapist for 15 weeks of the year. He retains Ryder Cup hopes but says he needs bigger results to improve his world ranking, and he will probably need a second place or a win in Dubai to earn a PGA Tour card. Calum Hill and Grant Forrest are the other Scots in the field, and Marc Warren returns to the DP World Tour via the Challenge Tour.

Golf.title: Rolex continues multi-year partnership with PGA Tour as Official Timekeeper
Golf.summary: Rolex continues multi-year partnership with PGA Tour as Official Timekeeper PGA Tour
bullets: The PGA Tour and Rolex announced on Wednesday a multi-year renewal of their Official Marketing Partnership, extending the Swiss watchmaker's position as Official Timekeeper of the PGA Tour. Rolex has sponsored the Tour since 2005 and will remain exclusive Official Timekeeper of the PGA Tour, PGA Tour Champions, the Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour Americas.

The agreement continues on-site, in-broadcast, social and digital integrations, and the showcasing of Rolex Testimonees such as Tiger Woods, Scottie Scheffler and Jackson Koivun. Rolex's association with golf dates to 1967, and it has been Official Timekeeper of the Presidents Cup since 2005 and a Global Partner since 2007. PGA Tour chief commercial officer Dhruv Prasad said the two have been partners for nearly three decades.
Golf.copy:
The PGA Tour and Rolex announced a multi-year renewal of their Official Marketing Partnership, extending the Swiss watchmaker’s position as Official Timekeeper of the PGA Tour. (Keyur Khamar/PGA Tour via Getty Images)

PONTE VEDRA BEACH, Fla., and GENEVA, Switzerland – The PGA Tour and Rolex announced Wednesday a multi-year renewal of their Official Marketing Partnership, extending the Swiss watchmaker’s position as Official Timekeeper of the PGA Tour. A sponsor of the Tour since 2005, Rolex will continue to bring its hallmark precision, performance and heritage of excellence to professional golf's biggest stage.

Golf.title: Carnoustie wins Open Championship bid, but there’s more to the story
Golf.summary: Carnoustie, one of the most difficult tests in pro golf, is set to host the Open Championship again. But what's different this time? The post Carnoustie wins Open Championship bid, but there’s more to the story appeared first on Golf .
bullets: The R&A announced on Monday that the Open Championship will return to Carnoustie Golf Links in 2029, the first time since 2018, when Francesco Molinari won and total attendance reached 172,000. Muirfield and Turnberry were passed over, with both reportedly presenting logistical issues around crowd space and transport.

Carnoustie's operations are now run by a consortium led by Max Herberstein, whose group bought the Carnoustie Golf Hotel for roughly £10m in 2023. In early 2025 it agreed with Angus Council and the charity running the courses to take over day-to-day golf operations for eight years. This year's Open at Royal Birkdale drew more than 300,000 spectators over eight days.
Golf.copy:
In 2029, the Open Championship will return to Carnoustie Golf Links, long heralded as one of the major’s most difficult venues. The decision, announced Monday by the R&A, feels like a no-brainer on its surface. Of course they’re headed back to one of the best golf courses on the planet.

But it came with secondary questions: Why go there before Muirfield? Or Turnberry? As the Open continues to grow in size, popularity and economic importance, decisions like this one are never just about revisiting an old stop on the event’s rota. Carnoustie’s placement, this time, is a much deeper conversation.

Golf.title: As LIV Golf fades away, one Jon Rahm question remains. He has a firm answer
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm is starting a new chapter of his career but one LIV Golf question keeps popping up. He has a firm answer. The post As LIV Golf fades away, one Jon Rahm question remains. He has a firm answer appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jon Rahm has said his poor major record since joining LIV Golf was down to his own swing problems and not the tour. Speaking ahead of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, he said people must stop blaming LIV. His comments follow LIV Golf's declaration in bankruptcy court last week that it would wind down operations, and Rahm's win in Abu Dhabi, his first outside LIV since his defection.

In three years on LIV, Rahm played 11 majors, with four top-10s and two missed cuts. In the three years before he left, he had seven top-10s in 12 majors, won two and missed no cuts. His only real chances came at the 2025 PGA Championship at Quail Hollow and the 2026 PGA at Aronimink, where Aaron Rai won. Rahm said he hopes his recent swing work will make him more consistent in majors.
Golf.copy:
In April of 2025, Jon Rahm said it was “unfair”. Rahm had been on LIV Golf for over a year and bemoaned being judged on his poor major record in 2024 rather than the overall state of his game, including his performance in LIV events.

“Consistency is something that I’ve always prided myself on. I think last year the state of my game was being unfairly judged based on how I played here and at the PGA compared to how I really played throughout the whole year,” Rahm said at Augusta National. “While I understand why, I don’t think it was the most fair state of my game. It’s something — top 10 statistics is something I’ve always prided myself on. Right before joining LIV, I think I was still close to 50 percent worldwide in all my starts finishing top 10, which is something I pride myself on, and to keep it going that way is not easy.”

Golf.title: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch
Golf.summary: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch Financier Worldwide
bullets: LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, as part of a restructuring support agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners Credit. The petition lists liabilities of $500m to $1bn and assets of $100m to $500m. The Public Investment Fund has agreed to provide $49.6m in debtor-in-possession financing during the court-supervised process, and BC Partners Credit and minority investors are expected to act as plan sponsors and provide exit financing.

The league intends to resume global team-based competition in 2027 under a revised ownership structure, subject to court approval and stakeholder support, and recent filings indicate players could hold a majority stake. The PIF said in April that it would stop funding the league after investing more than $5bn, and at least $45m is believed to be owed to players. Chief executive Scott O'Neil said the process gives the league time to pursue a transaction built around fans and a player-first ownership model.
Golf.copy:
Controversial breakaway golf league LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey as part of a restructuring agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners that it hopes will secure the league’s future beyond 2026.

The organisation, which created significant division within professional golf following its launch in 2022, reported liabilities of between $500m and $1bn and assets of between $100m and $500m in its Chapter 11 petition.

LIV Golf: What next for Bryson DeChambeau? How YouTube star can boost major hopes with return to traditional men's tours Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley believes Bryson DeChambeau needs to return to golf’s traditional tours to boost his hopes of winning majors again.

DeChambeau's competitive future remains uncertain, following the demise of LIV Golf, with no pathway currently in place for an immediate return to the PGA Tour and no confirmation of how frequently he plans to tee it up in 2027.
